note: Third-party plugin and theme catalogues, gathered by fetching each URL. The client lists and opens them; only its own documented addon dialect (docs/addon-framework.md) can be installed here, so a source being reachable is not a promise that an addon from it runs.

sources.name: Aliucord plugin manifest
sources.notes: Every published Aliucord plugin: name, version, metadata and the ZIP artifact URL, in one array. The most useful single Android source; the artifacts are prebuilt ZIPs, not source.

sources.name: Aliucord plugins source tree
sources.notes: GitHub Contents API JSON for the official monorepo, plugin sources under plugins/<plugin>/. Unauthenticated and rate-limited, so the manifest above is the better default.

sources.name: Aliucord verified repository (legacy)
sources.notes: The fetched central verified repository, including legacy and React Native plugins. Its README points at a data branch rather than publishing a machine-readable index, so this is one to read, not to parse.

sources.name: Aliucord builds branch (gone)
sources.notes: This branch URL 404ed when fetched. It is kept as its own entry so a browser that tries the old builds path can say the source is gone instead of showing an empty list as if the ecosystem were empty.

sources.name: Aliucord themes (community)
sources.notes: There is no official Aliucord theme index and the themes page is view-only, so this is a directory listing of one community theme repository; each theme is its own JSON file, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/catppuccin/aliucord/main/src/catppuccin-mocha-blue.json. Rate-limited when unauthenticated. Enumerating the tree is mechanical; finding themes in the first place is not.

sources.name: Aliucord themes page
sources.notes: The official listing, fetched, and it is a rendered view-only page - the fetched text exposed only its title, so there is nothing here a program should parse.

sources.name: Aliucord repositories (org API)
sources.notes: GitHub REST API JSON listing every repository the Aliucord organisation owns. Good for discovering what the project maintains; it cannot see third-party authors' plugins, and it is rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: Vendetta proxy plugin list (legacy)
sources.notes: A JSON array of plugin URL strings from the Vendetta plugin proxy. Vendetta itself was discontinued in 2024, so treat this as a legacy snapshot rather than a maintained feed.

sources.name: Vendetta proxy plugin metadata (legacy)
sources.notes: The same Vendetta list with metadata objects rather than bare URLs. Legacy, as above.

sources.name: Vendetta plugin browser (legacy)
sources.notes: A rendered browser over the proxy lists, fetched but only its title came out. Useful as a thing to open in the built-in browser; there is nothing here a program should parse.

sources.name: Vendetta plugin organisations (legacy)
sources.notes: The organisation page listing the proxy, scripts and web repositories, with visible activity only in 2023-2024. Vendetta is discontinued; this is a rendered listing, not a JSON index.

sources.name: Bunny proxy plugin list (legacy)
sources.notes: Same shape as the Vendetta list, with some Bunny-patched entries. Bunny is archived and unmaintained.

sources.name: Bunny proxy plugin metadata (legacy)
sources.notes: The Bunny list with metadata objects. Includes entries hosted under rico040.github.io/bunny-plugins/.

sources.name: Bunny per-plugin manifest (example)
sources.notes: Fetched example of how one author publishes a single plugin: a manifest.json beside the plugin, not an entry in a central index. This is also the shape of a hand-added source URL.

sources.name: Bunny plugin browser (legacy)
sources.notes: The bn-plugins fork of the Vendetta proxy browser, fetched and again only its title came out. Pyoncord was archived in 2025, so whether the list behind it is complete is unverified.

sources.name: Rico040 Bunny plugins (author)
sources.notes: A README list of plugin names and install URLs for Vendetta plugins the author patched for Bunny. A per-author listing, not a central index, and Bunny itself is archived.

sources.name: Pyoncord organisation (archived)
sources.notes: The organisation page says it was archived on 2025-08-07 and is no longer maintained. Useful for historical provenance; it publishes no addon index of its own, and its legacy browsing overlaps the Vendetta and Bunny sources above.

sources.name: Revenge community catalogue
sources.notes: The maintained mobile catalogue: plugin id, version, channel, artifact URL and SHA-256 digest per entry. In this ecosystem themes are plugins, so one list covers both kinds. Mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenge-mod/revenge-community-plugins/gh-pages/index.json

sources.name: Revenge catalogue (raw mirror)
sources.notes: The same index from the raw host, which is the form to prefer on a device where the pages domain is blocked. Plugin ids, descriptions, authors, channels, versions, ZIP URLs, SHA-256 hashes and dependencies.

sources.name: Revenge community plugins repo
sources.notes: The repository behind the catalogue, sources under plugins/<plugin>/ and the published index on gh-pages. Browseable; read the index.json above instead of walking this.

sources.name: Revenge repository contents (API)
sources.notes: GitHub REST API JSON array of the repository root, including plugins/ and repo.config.json. Enumerating it works; it is not as convenient as the published index, and it is rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: Revenge repository branches (API)
sources.notes: GitHub REST API JSON array of branch names and commit metadata; the fetched response confirmed gh-pages and main. Rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: Revenge repositories (org API)
sources.notes: GitHub REST API JSON for every repository the Revenge organisation owns, tooling included. Discovery, not an addon catalogue, and rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: Revenge plugin format template
sources.notes: Plain text documenting the monorepo layout (plugins/<name>/) and the static index.json a repository publishes on gh-pages, with artifact URLs and checksums. The best description of what a Revenge-compatible index contains; it is prose, so nothing parses it.

sources.name: Revenge Plugins List (community)
sources.notes: A status and listing site for Revenge plugins and themes. Not affiliated with or maintained by Revenge, and it publishes no raw index, so nothing should parse it.

sources.name: Revenge Plugins List source tree
sources.notes: GitHub REST API JSON tree of the tracker site's source, including src/Themes. It enumerates files rather than installable addon metadata, and it is rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: Nexpid's Revenge plugins (author)
sources.notes: An author-maintained list whose site at https://revenge.nexpid.xyz/index.json returned 404, so it is a page for a person, not a catalogue for a program. It lists 19 plugins with finished, broken, unfinished and discontinued statuses; Cloud Sync and Themes+ cover theme work.

sources.name: Nexpid's Revenge plugins source
sources.notes: The repository behind the list, a README of per-author status rather than an index. Maintenance is mixed, so an entry being listed does not mean it works today.

sources.name: Siguma's plugins (author)
sources.notes: A README naming plugins and their install pages, several maintained from Vendetta for Revenge and Kettu. A per-author listing, not an official index.

sources.name: kmmiio99o plugins (author)
sources.notes: A README list the author states is for Kettu, Revenge and ShiggyCord, with individually hosted install URLs. Per-author and of uncertain maintenance.

sources.name: Kettu
sources.notes: A continuation of Bunny whose GitHub repository is a mirror, with contributions directed to Codeberg. No Kettu-owned plugin or theme index was found, so this is a project page, not a catalogue.

sources.name: ShiggyCord
sources.notes: A Kettu-based mobile bundle documenting a release bundle URL and build steps. A bundle is not an addon catalogue; no machine-readable ShiggyCord index was verified.

sources.name: Catppuccin themes (legacy clients)
sources.notes: A README documenting JSON theme files in a themes directory, and stating support for Bunny, Revenge and Enmity while noting Vendetta is end-of-life. The individual theme file was not separately fetched, so treat the per-theme URLs as repository contents rather than a verified index.

sources.name: Enmity (iOS)
sources.notes: The iOS client whose ecosystem also serves Vendetta-lineage addons. The fetched page describes plugins and themes but publishes no catalogue or index, and its 2026 maintenance is unclear.

sources.name: Enmity addons browser (iOS)
sources.notes: A rendered addon listing with names, authors, descriptions and install buttons. It says explicitly that it does not work inside Discord's built-in browser, which matters for a client whose catalogue is opened in one; no machine-readable endpoint was verified.

sources.name: spinfal Enmity plugins (author)
sources.notes: A README list with compiled and source links; the author states the repository is no longer in development and cannot be kept working. Historical.

sources.name: Fifi's Enmity addon store
sources.notes: One author's store, generated with enmity-store. Its generated data format was not verified and it is not a global Enmity registry.

sources.name: Mortyick Enmity themes (author)
sources.notes: A README listing theme names and URLs with files under themes/. The author says no new Enmity-specific themes are planned. A human list; no raw theme file was separately fetched.

sources.name: Vencord plugin sources
sources.notes: Directory listing of the Vencord plugin tree. These are TypeScript sources in the repository, not installable artifacts, and https://vencord.dev/plugins is a rendered page rather than an index. Rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: Vencord plugin tree (page)
sources.notes: The same directory as the API entry above, as a rendered GitHub page. Built-in plugins live under src/plugins/; this is source code, not an install catalogue.

sources.name: Vencord plugin catalogue (page)
sources.notes: The official catalogue page with names, authors, descriptions and filters. Useful to open; no JSON manifest or public catalogue API was verified behind it.

sources.name: Vencord source projects
sources.notes: A rendered list of Vencord repositories, including the main source and Vesktop, which confirms the project relationships. It is not an addon listing.

sources.name: Vencord plugin readmes
sources.notes: JSON mapping plugin names to README text. Useful for descriptions; it is not a catalogue of installable artifacts and carries no download URLs.

sources.name: Vencord plugins on GitHub (topic)
sources.notes: Community discovery through GitHub topic tags, which authors apply unevenly. Incomplete by construction and a rendered listing; useful for finding a repository, not for a catalogue.

sources.name: D3SOX userplugins (author)
sources.notes: A README list of the author's plugins with install instructions; the author states the collection is unmaintained and provided as-is. A useful example of a per-author Vencord plugin repository.

sources.name: Equicord plugin metadata
sources.notes: Generated metadata for the combined Equicord catalogue, which includes the Vencord plugins it ships. Metadata and source paths only; there are no plugin ZIPs.

sources.name: Equicord-only plugin metadata
sources.notes: The Equicord-specific half of the catalogue, from src/equicordplugins/. Same shape and same limitation: metadata, not artifacts.

sources.name: Equicord's Vencord plugin metadata
sources.notes: The Vencord half as Equicord builds it, from src/plugins/. Metadata only.

sources.name: Equicord/Vencord theme library
sources.notes: A community theme and snippet library serving Equicord and Vencord, with descriptions and update information in the page. No public JSON theme index was verified, so it is a site to open rather than a catalogue to read.

sources.name: BetterDiscord plugins page
sources.notes: The listing is rendered in the page and there is no verified public raw catalogue endpoint; BetterDiscord addons are single files hosted by their authors, not a shared repository.

sources.name: BetterDiscord themes page
sources.notes: Same page-only situation as the plugin listing above. Open it in the built-in browser; do not scrape it in code.

sources.name: BetterDiscord plugins on GitHub (topic)
sources.notes: A rendered topic page of tagged repositories. Community discovery only: tags are user-applied and incomplete, and it is not a curated index.

sources.name: BetterDiscord themes on GitHub (topic)
sources.notes: The theme half of the same topic-tag discovery, with the same incompleteness. A rendered page, not a trusted theme store.

sources.name: DiscordStyles organisation
sources.notes: An organisation page of CSS and SCSS themes and tooling, with repository activity visible in 2026. An org-level listing a person reads, not a unified theme manifest.

sources.name: DiscordStyles ThemeRepo (gone)
sources.notes: A commonly assumed theme index repository that 404ed when fetched. Recorded so a client that guesses this path reports a missing source rather than an empty theme list.

sources.name: DiscordStyles PluginRepo (gone)
sources.notes: The plugin-side version of the same guess, also 404 when fetched. Not a verified plugin index.

sources.name: BetterDiscord repositories (org API)
sources.notes: GitHub REST API JSON for the organisation's own repositories - the mod, the CLI and tooling - not third-party plugin or theme entries. Rate-limited when unauthenticated.

sources.name: BetterDiscord CLI
sources.notes: A README documenting bdcli commands that search the store and manage local plugins and themes. It shows the store can be queried, but it is a desktop command-line tool - not an endpoint this client's browser can reach.

sources.name: BetterDiscord CLI documentation
sources.notes: Rendered documentation for the CLI, less current than the repository README on store browsing. Not an addon index.

sources.name: Replugged store
sources.notes: A store UI over per-addon manifests; no public raw index was verified. Themes beyond the store are arbitrary CSS URLs with no central catalogue anywhere in this ecosystem.
